title: Succinct noninteractive arguments for all NP from LWE alone
formal: Does standard polynomial-hard Learning With Errors suffice for succinct noninteractive arguments for every NP relation in the honestly generated CRS model, without another computational or proof-complexity assumption?
definitions: An NP relation has polynomial-time verification and polynomially bounded witnesses. A SNARG has a polynomial-time prover and verifier and a common reference string generated before the statement; proof length must be polynomial in the security parameter and logarithm of the computation length. Soundness must hold against polynomial-size adversaries for all sufficiently large security parameters, not merely infinitely often. No knowledge-extraction or zero-knowledge property is demanded.

context_blocks.text: Succinct arguments compress the evidence for a potentially long computation into a short message. Basing them on a standard lattice assumption would connect a powerful verification primitive to a much more established cryptographic foundation.

The June 2026 source obtains SNARGs for NP from LWE, SXDH, derandomization and a proof-complexity assumption together. Those additional hypotheses matter. Results for restricted NP subclasses or infinitely-often soundness do not settle the target for all NP.

why: A major minimal-assumption question for general succinct verification.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
